# Y8960 hardware

> This is an English translation of the [Japanese original](../hardware.md). Where the two differ, the Japanese version is authoritative.

The parts this driver depends on, extracted from `doc/manual` (the programmer's manual) and `doc/spec` (the specification `Y8960_Specifications.xlsx`) of [Y8960_Cartridge](https://github.com/hra1129/Y8960_Cartridge). The assembly-side definitions are in
`src/inc/y8960hw.inc`.

**The source of these copies is the 2026-10-20 version of the specification (the version that includes OPM; `500fbd5` of Y8960_Cartridge).** The specification sometimes indicates deletions with strikethrough, which cannot be seen when only the cell values are read.

## Sound chips on board

| Block | Equivalent | Instances |
|---|---|---|
| SSGS | Two YM2149-compatible SSG instances, with per-channel volume and panning added | 1 |
| OPLL-EX | YM2413 + per-channel independent preset voice bank + per-channel panning | 1 |
| OPL2-EX | YM3812 + ADPCM-B (Y8950-compatible) + per-channel and ADPCM panning | 1 |
| SCC | Konami SCC + per-channel panning | 1 |
| OPM | YM2151-compatible (IKAOPM). **Not compatible with SFG-01/05** (see below) | 1 |
| Digital Mixer | Combines the volumes of the blocks inside the FPGA. Panning is held by each block | 1 |

**Each block's clock is the same as the MSX standard.** The Y8960 is designed as an upgrade path for the MSX standard sound chips, so each block is supplied with the same clock as the chip it replaces. The primary sources do not state the values; this was confirmed as the design intent.

| Block | Clock |
|---|--:|
| SSGS | 1.7897725MHz (`3.579545 / 2`) |
| OPLL-EX / OPL2-EX / SCC / OPM | 3.579545MHz |

The tuning tables follow from these. Both the OPL-family phase increments and the SSG and SCC divider values are computed with these values. The OPM clock was read from a comment in the RTL (`src/ikaopm_patch/opm.v`) and is not written in the specification.

ADPCM memory is 256KB, and OPL2-EX (one instance) uses all of it.

## Memory map

The on-board memory is 256KB. It is divided into 8KB pieces from the start and given bank numbers: **#0-#15 are ROM, #16-#31 are RAM**.

The MSX sees four windows, and any bank number can be switched into each of them.

| Window | Address |
|---|---|
| BANK0 | `4000h`-`5FFFh` (also mirrored at `C000h`-`DFFFh`) |
| BANK1 | `6000h`-`7FFFh` |
| BANK2 | `8000h`-`9FFFh` |
| BANK3 | `A000h`-`BFFFh` |

The initial values at power-on and at reset are BANK0=#0, BANK1=#1, BANK2=#2, BANK3=#3.

Even when a RAM bank is switched in, writes to that location have no effect in the initial state.
To write to it, you must switch to RAM mode. It works by switching because the memory-mapped I/O
is at the same location.

## RAM mode and bank registers

Bit0 of `4FFBh` is the RAM mode. It is mirrored at `4XFBh` (X=8-F), and
**this block is the only one that is always visible in both modes**.

| Mode | Bank registers | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| RAM mode 0 (compatibility mode) | `5000-57FFh` BANK0, `7000-77FFh` BANK1, `9000-97FFh` BANK2, `B000-B7FFh` BANK3 | The sound chip MMIO is visible |
| RAM mode 1 | `4FFCh` BANK0, `4FFDh` BANK1, `4FFEh` BANK2, `4FFFh` BANK3 | Writes to RAM banks go through |

## Memory-mapped I/O (sound chip registers)

| Address | Contents |
|---|---|
| `7FF0h` / `7FF1h` | SSGS address / data |
| `7FF2h` / `7FF3h` | OPL2 address / data |
| `7FF4h` / `7FF5h` | OPLL address / data |
| `7FF6h` | I/O Enabler 1: bit0 OPLL |
| `7FF7h` | Digital Mixer: SSGS volume |
| `7FF8h` | Digital Mixer: OPLL volume |
| `7FF9h` | Digital Mixer: OPL2 volume (including ADPCM) |
| `7FFAh` | Digital Mixer: SCC volume |
| `7FFBh` / `7FFCh` | OPM address / data |
| `7FFDh` | Digital Mixer: OPM volume |
| `7FFEh` | Digital Mixer: master volume |
| `7FFFh` | I/O Enabler 2: bit0 OPL2, bit1 SSG, bit2 OPM, bit7 TIMER. Not mirrored. Readable (see below) |

**A Digital Mixer volume of 0 mutes, and 128 is the maximum.** 1-127 is a linear gain of value ÷ 128, and if bit7 is set it is the maximum (the fork side's records, based on an answer from the hardware side). The master volume uses the same scale. ADPCM is mixed into OPL2, and then the OPL2 volume is applied to it. **The reset value of all six is 128** (not stated in the specification. For the four blocks this is an answer from the hardware side, and for the master it was settled by the user. 2026-10-18. For OPM, per the 2026-10-20 entry in Y8960_Cartridge's `history.md`). **Only the OPM volume is at a separate address** — `7FFBh` `7FFCh`, which follow the four blocks, are the OPM address and data.

All except `7FFFh` are write-only. **They appear only in RAM mode 0, or when a ROM bank is switched into BANK1.** Switching a RAM bank into BANK1 makes them disappear.

**`7FFFh` will become readable** (an answer from the hardware side, 2026-10-26; at the time of the answer it was not in the RTL). Only `7FFFh` is readable; the other addresses, including `7FF6h`, remain write-only. The answer does not say what the unused bits (bit3-6) read as, or whether, as with writes, it can be read only while the window is switched in ([Open questions](#open-questions)).

So that multiple Y8960s can be controlled individually, the regular I/O ports are disabled right after startup and right after reset, and become enabled only when the I/O Enabler is written. This is the same idea as the Panasonic FMPAC.

## Regular I/O ports

Enabled after the I/O Enabler is written.

| Port | Contents |
|---|---|
| `A0h` / `A1h` | SSGS address / write |
| `7Ch` / `7Dh` | OPLL address / data |
| `C0h` / `C1h` | OPL2 address / data |
| `7Eh` / `7Fh` | OPM address / data. Reading `7Fh` returns the status |

**`A2h` is the read port of the internal PSG, and the cartridge does not respond to it** (confirmed with the hardware side, 2026-10-16). All SSGS registers are write-only, and the BASIC extension keeps a copy of what it writes.

**SSGS has the two SSG instances and the block's own registers on a single port pair.** The register number decides which one a write reaches.

| Register | Contents |
|---|---|
| `00h`-`0Fh` | SSG1. Same layout as YM2149. `0Eh` `0Fh` (GPIO) are not connected |
| `10h`-`1Fh` | SSG2. Same layout. The low 4 bits of `1Fh` are the on-board LEDs |
| `20h`-`22h` / `24h`-`26h` | Volume of channels A/B/C of SSG1 / SSG2. 0-128, 128 is the maximum, default 128. **Linear gain** |
| `28h`-`2Ah` / `2Ch`-`2Eh` | Panning of channels A/B/C of SSG1 / SSG2. 1 is far left, 128 is center, 255 is far right. Default 128 |
| `23h` `27h` `2Bh` `2Fh`, `30h` and above | Not connected |

**A panning value of 0 is not in the specification.** The RTL, in the panning table shared by all blocks, treats it as far left, the same as 1, and the fork followed it (the fork side's records, 2026-10-19). This BASIC extension gives 0 no meaning; if 0 is written, it is passed to the register as is.

**Panning is distributed by power panning.** With θ = (value − 1) / 254 × π/2, L = cos θ and R = sin θ. At the center, both left and right are 1/√2. That the gain is linear, and the distribution law, are not in the primary sources; they are decisions of the hardware side received via the user (2026-10-16).

**The internal PSG responds only when the upper 4 bits of the register number are 0** — writes to `10h` and above reach only SSGS (some emulators do not behave this way: on openMSX for machines other than turbo R, and on blueMSX for all machines, the internal PSG also responds to these numbers).

SCC has no I/O ports and is controlled only through memory-mapped I/O.

## SCC registers

Writing `3Fh` to a bank register makes the SCC registers appear in that window instead of a memory bank. The bank value is the same as on Konami SCC cartridges, and the position within the window is also the same as the original (`9800h` for the `8000h`-`9FFFh` window): `1800h` from the start. This driver switches it into the BANK2 window, so it starts at `9800h`.

**It can be switched into BANK2 and BANK1 only. Into BANK2 in either mode, and into BANK1 only in RAM mode 1.** When switched into BANK1, the addresses are `7800h`-`7FFFh`. `9000h` in RAM mode 0 and `4FFEh` in RAM mode 1 write to the same BANK2 bank register. This driver switches it into BANK2 in RAM mode 1.

The sources are the RTL (`IKASCC_vrc_s.v` of v0.9.3; only read) and the user (2026-10-21). blueMSX-plus_Y8960 also implements the same conditions (`sccVisible` in `romMapperY8960Scc.c`). openMSX_Y8960 switches it into any of the BANK0-3 windows, so this makes no difference to the tests of this driver, which uses BANK2. The text of the 2026-10-20 version of the specification says "BANK2 in RAM mode 0, BANK1 in RAM mode 1" and does not mention BANK2 in RAM mode 1.

| Offset | Contents |
|---|---|
| `+000h`-`07Fh` | Waveform memory. 32 bytes×4 blocks. ch3 and ch4 share the last block |
| `+080h`-`089h` | Frequency. 2 bytes per channel×5 channels |
| `+08Ah`-`08Eh` | Volume. 5 channels, 0-15 |
| `+08Fh` | Channel ON/OFF. bit0-4 |
| `+0E0h`-`0FFh` | deformation register |

**Panning is at `+100h`-`+104h` (channels A-E) of the SCC register window** — `9900h`-`9904h` when switched into BANK2, `7900h`-`7904h` for BANK1. It is a Y8960 addition and write-only. The scale and distribution are the same as SSGS, default 128. The SCC itself looks only at the low 8 bits, so the cartridge does not pass writes to these five addresses to the SCC (if it did, they would land in the waveform at `+000h`-`+004h`). Reads, and `+105h` and above, are mirrors of the SCC as before. **It can be written in RAM mode too** — the 2026-10-19 RTL discarded writes in RAM mode, but the 2026-10-20 RTL (`scc.v`) accepts them whenever the SCC window is switched in, without looking at the mode (only read).

This bank value and layout are the Konami SCC specification, not something confirmed in the Y8960 primary sources. The driver is arranged so that it can follow a change by rewriting `SCC_BANK` (bank value), `SCC_WINOFF` (position within the window) and `SCC_O_*` (offset of each register within the block) in `src/inc/y8960hw.inc`.

## OPLL-EX registers

`00h`-`3Fh` are the same as YM2413. `40h`-`48h` and `50h`-`58h` are Y8960 additions; in both, one register corresponds to each of ch0-ch8. In `40h`-`48h`, bit1-0 select that channel's preset voice bank, and `50h`-`58h` are that channel's panning (1 is far left, 128 is center, 255 is far right. Default 128. The distribution is power panning, the same as SSGS). `0Fh` is the TEST register; always write 0 to it.

**The panning of the rhythm sounds is inherited as is from the panning of their original channels 6-8** (a decision of the hardware side, 2026-10-16). Following the YM2413 assignment, BD uses `56h`, HH and SD use `57h`, and TOM and TCY use `58h`. **The mix ratio of melodic sounds to rhythm sounds is 1:1.**

| Value | Preset |
|--:|---|
| 0 | OPLL (YM2413) |
| 1 | OPLL-X (YM2423 equivalent) |
| 2 | OPLL-P (YMF281 equivalent) |
| 3 | VRC7 (DS1001 equivalent) |

Bit4-3 of voice register `03h` are DC / DM (waveform select).

A plain YM2413 does not update its address latch unless bit7-6 of the address are 00, and also discards the data write that follows, so on hardware without the extensions, writes to `40h` and above are simply ignored and do not corrupt the user voice registers.

## OPL2-EX registers

Same layout as MSX-AUDIO (Y8950). The waveform select at `E0h`-`F5h` is the addition in OPL2. The keyboard I/F at `05h`/`06h`, the prescale at `0Dh`/`0Eh`, and the DAC and I/O registers at `15h`-`1Ah` are removed.

`F6h`-`FEh` are the panning of channels 1-9 and `FFh` is the ADPCM panning; these are Y8960 additions. Only this section counts channels from 1. Counting from 0 as in the OPLL-EX section, they are channels 0-8, and the rhythm sounds correspond to 6-8. The scale and distribution are the same as SSGS (default 128). **The rhythm sounds inherit the panning of their original channels 7-9** (the same as OPLL; the fork side's records). The mix ratio of melodic sounds to rhythm sounds is 1:1.

`E0h`-`F5h` take effect only when bit5 (WSE) of `01h` is set, as on the YM3812. When it is clear, all operators produce a sine wave. `MINIT` sets it when initializing the block.

## OPM registers

Same layout as YM2151, with no Y8960 additions. The specification's sheet lists only the ports (I/O `7Eh`/`7Fh`, memory-mapped I/O `7FFBh`/`7FFCh`) and has no register table.

**It is not compatible with SFG-01/05.** The SFG's YM2151 appears in its own slot's memory at `3FF0h`/`3FF1h`, so software written for the SFG cannot play this OPM. There is also nothing corresponding to the SFG's YM2148 (MIDI and keyboard).

**Panning is only the chip's RL bits (bit7-6 of `20h`-`27h`).** There are no per-channel panning registers like those of SSGS and the others.

**Writes need no wait.** The cartridge has a 16-entry write queue in front of the port and sends the writes to the chip one at a time (leaving 8 clocks after an address and 80 clocks after data). While the queue is full, it stops the CPU with `/WAIT`. Reading `7Fh` returns the status, and bit7 (busy) is also set while entries remain in the queue. Bit1-0 are the timer flags. Per the 2026-10-20 entry in Y8960_Cartridge's `history.md` and `opm.v`.

**The timer interrupt is connected to `/INT`** (same entry). If bit2 of I/O Enabler 2 is closed, it is only the ports that do not answer; whether the chip's timer raises an interrupt is decided by the chip's register (`14h`).

**Bit2 of I/O Enabler 2 is 0 after reset** (the ports are closed).

## Interrupts

The MSX-TIMER and the OPL2 built-in timer can generate interrupts. Neither reaches the MSX computer unless bit7 of I/O Enabler 2 is open. The OPM timer can also raise interrupts (see above).

### MSX-TIMER

**This driver takes the sequencer tick from here** (it sets the period from the tempo), so it needs the register layout and how the period is determined.

**The port assignment is settled.** It is not yet reflected in the manual, but it has been confirmed with the people building the hardware (2026-09-09, `doc/fork/y8960/implementation-plan.md` of `openMSX_Y8960`).

| Port | Contents |
|---|---|
| `B0h` | Register number. bit3-2 = counter number 0-3, bit1-0 = register number 0-2 within that counter |
| `B1h` | Read/write of the register selected with `B0h` |
| `B2h` | Interrupt flags. On read, bit *n* = counter *n*. Bits written with 1 are cleared |
| `B3h` | On write, counter select 0-3; on read, the current value of that counter (8bit) |

Each counter has 3 registers.

| Register | Contents |
|---|---|
| 0 | bit0 = repeat (0 one-shot / 1 repeat), bit6-4 = resolution 0-7, bit7 = interrupt enable |
| 1 | Compare value (8bit) |
| 2 | bit0 = count enable; writing 1 to bit1 returns the counter to 0 |

The period is **(compare value+1) × unit**, and the unit is **2^(10 + 2×resolution) ÷ clock**. Each step up in resolution multiplies the unit by 4, so the 8 steps span a factor of 2^14.

**The contents of a counter's registers are not included in the confirmed table.** The three above are copied from `src/sound/MSXTimer.cc` of `openMSX_Y8960`, which inherited them from buppu3's implementation.

**The reference clock is 85,909,080Hz** (3.579545MHz×24). The unit for each resolution is therefore as follows.

| Resolution | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Unit | 11.9µs | 47.7µs | 191µs | 763µs | 3.05ms | 12.2ms | 48.8ms | 195ms |

The compare value is 8bit, so the longest period is 256×195ms = 50 seconds.

**Where this comes from.** The implementation in `src/sound/MSXTimer` of `openMSX_Y8960`. `doc/fork/y8960/hardware-notes.md` §6 of the same repository says "71.5µs - 1.17s", but **the fork side confirmed that it is that document that is wrong and the implementation that is right** (2026-09-10).

## Open questions

Things needed to implement this driver that are not stated in the primary sources, or that have not been confirmed.

**The hardware is under development, and the primary sources are still catching up.** The copies above may disagree with each other, or with information obtained by other routes. In that case, the copies are not corrected by guesswork; the disagreement is listed here.

| | |
|---|---|
| Recommended initialization sequence | The relevant section of the manual is not yet written |
| Minimum wait for register writes | The relevant section of the manual is not yet written. Currently secured with the equivalent of `JR $+2` |
| OPM clock | 3.579545MHz was read from a comment in the RTL and is not in the specification |
| Reading `7FFFh` | There is only an answer that it will be made readable; it is not yet in the RTL or the specification. The values of the unused bits (bit3-6), and whether it can be read when the window is not switched in, are unknown |
